children: Brazil's government on Thursday widened its forecast for this year's primary deficit to 80.9 billion reais ($15.61 billion) from 52 billion reais projected in July, a shortfall equivalent to 0.59% of gross domestic product (GDP).
Deterioration reflects a 22.1 billion-real increase in projected spending and a 15.7 billion-real decline in total expected revenue.
Government estimates that primary spending will end the year at 19.55% of GDP, the highest level of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's current term, which began in 2023.
Rising spending lies at the heart of fiscal concerns surrounding Lula's administration as the leftist leader seeks re-election in October.
Investor skepticism about Brazil's ability to restore fiscal balance has driven up risk premiums, contributing to a sharp increase in the gross debt-to-GDP ratio.

This year's fiscal target is a primary surplus of 0.25% of GDP, with a tolerance band of 0.25 percentage point, though the government is allowed to exclude certain expenditures when assessing compliance.
Using that methodology, it projected a primary deficit of 0.1% of GDP, compared with a surplus forecast of 0.08% of GDP in its previous revenue and expenditure report.
To comply with fiscal rules, the government said it would need to freeze 13.6 billion reais in spending and block 2.4 billion reais in expenditures.
